title: Why 36 subscribers left, on one wall
variant: A wall you can re-sort, and it remembers where you put things
prompt: Take the free-text answers from our cancellation survey and lay them out as an affinity board rather than summarizing them.
note: The workshop shape, and the cover because it is the one that reads as a whiteboard at a glance. Position is a judgment rather than a measurement, which is exactly why every note carries `data-drag`: a reader who disagrees with a placement can act on it instead of only noting it, and the page says outright that their arrangement lives in their browser and never in the file. Color is a second dimension that the clusters do not encode -- whether the person said they would come back -- so the wall answers a question a six-bar chart of the same survey cannot. The sixth region holds the four answers that would not sit anywhere, which the findings treat as a result rather than as leftovers.
